record.original_question: For integers q >= p >= 3, what is the maximum spectral radius among graphs in G(m, theta_{1,p,q})? Equivalently, characterize the extremal graphs with m edges that avoid the theta graph formed by three internally disjoint paths of lengths 1, p, and q between the same two endpoints.

evidence.quote: Problem 8 (Li, Zhao and Zou [17], 2025). What is the maximum spectral radius of graphs among G(m, theta1,p,q) for q >= p >= 3?
Theorem 3.36 together with Theorem 3.27 solve Problem 8 completely.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For integers $q \ge p \ge 3$, the theta graph $\theta_{1,p,q}$ is the graph obtained from two distinct vertices $u,v$ by joining them with three internally disjoint paths of lengths $1$, $p$, and $q$ (so $\theta_{1,p,q}$ has the edge $uv$ together with two internally disjoint $u$-$v$ paths of lengths $p$ and $q$). For a positive integer $m$, let $\mathcal{G}(m, \theta_{1,p,q})$ denote the family of simple graphs with exactly $m$ edges that contain no subgraph isomorphic to $\theta_{1,p,q}$. The spectral radius $\rho(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix.

Determine, for all integers $q \ge p \ge 3$ and all sufficiently large $m$, the maximum value of $\rho(G)$ over $G \in \mathcal{G}(m, \theta_{1,p,q})$, and characterize all graphs attaining this maximum.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, posed by Li, Zhao and Zou (2025) as Problem 8 concerning the maximum spectral radius among $\theta_{1,p,q}$-free graphs with $m$ edges, has reportedly been resolved completely; a recent survey/paper indicates that two of its theorems (corresponding to Theorem 3.27 and Theorem 3.36) together solve this problem. Independent confirmation via search was limited, so the resolution rests on this single source.
